review.summary: This patch tries to do at least three things at once: change ACL root semantics from a bool to a namespace pointer, add an ErrNamespaceSealed sentinel with a stubbed Core.NamespaceSealed, and mass-rewrite test contexts. That's THREE-PATCHES territory. The ACL change is the load-bearing one and it's the one with the bug: AllowOperation uses ns.HasParent(a.root) which, by every sane reading, asks "is a.root an ancestor of ns?" — but the prior check forbade root policies outside the root namespace, and now it allows them anywhere and grants root privileges across any namespace whose ancestry includes the policy's namespace. Combined with a stubbed NamespaceSealed that just returns false, you've shipped a security-adjacent surface change with the actual enforcement turned off. Refuse until the seal manager exists and the HasParent direction is proven correct with tests covering siblings, cousins, and the root-policy-from-child case.

issues.description: Core.NamespaceSealed is a stub returning false while ACL/list paths already depend on it
issues.detail: Adding a method that unconditionally returns false and wiring ListAllNamespaces and root-token paths to depend on it is shipping a security-relevant hole with a TODO on top. The PR description says 'currently stubbed, until SealManager introduction' — fine, but then the call sites that depend on the truthful answer should not land yet either. Land the stub and its consumers in the same patch as the real implementation, or gate the consumers behind a feature flag. Right now any future bug where a sealed namespace must be excluded is silently broken.

issues.description: ACL root semantics changed from bool to namespace pointer with unverified HasParent direction
issues.detail: Previously: root policy only allowed in root namespace, fast-path was unambiguous. Now: a.root holds the namespace the root policy was created in, and AllowOperation does `if !ns.HasParent(a.root) { return ret }` then grants RootPrivs. The direction matters: is this 'is a.root an ancestor of ns' (root policy from parent grants root in child — plausible) or the reverse (root policy from child grants root in parent — catastrophic)? The test only covers ns1 with no real hierarchy. Add explicit tests for: root-ns policy used in child (should allow), child-ns policy used in root (must deny), child-ns policy used in sibling (must deny), child-ns policy used in deeper descendant (decide and document). Until those tests exist and pass, the fast-path is not safe to ship.

issues.description: Patch does three unrelated things — THREE-PATCHES
issues.detail: 1) ACL root-namespace refactor. 2) ErrNamespaceSealed sentinel and Core.NamespaceSealed stub. 3) Mass test context rewrites from context.Background() to namespace.RootContext(t.Context()). Each is independently reviewable; mashed together they hide the real change (the ACL semantics flip) in a sea of test churn. Split. The reviewer-six-months-from-now bisecting a regression will curse this commit.

issues.description: response_util.go refactor changes control flow, not just style
issues.detail: The old code was a sequence of independent `if` checks — multiple could fire and the last one wins. The new code is a `switch` with `case` clauses — only the first match fires. For ErrSealed + body-too-large or APILocked + HTTPCoded, the resulting status code can differ from before. That may be the intended behavior, but it's not called out in the description and there's no test. Either justify the semantic change in the commit message and add a test, or keep it as sequential ifs and just add the new sentinel.

issues.description: errwrap.Contains on error message string for sentinel matching is fragile
issues.detail: `errwrap.Contains(err, consts.ErrNamespaceSealed.Error())` matches by string content, which is exactly the wrong way to identify a sentinel — any wrapped error whose message happens to contain 'namespace is sealed' triggers a 503. Use errors.Is. This is an existing pattern in the file for ErrSealed, but propagating bad taste isn't a justification; the new sentinel should use the modern check.

issues.description: NSTokenLength = TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID is unreadable cleverness
issues.detail: Indexing a string literal to get a byte to add to an int to express 'one byte for a dot separator' is the kind of cleverness that looks fine when you write it and is hostile when someone else reads it. `TokenLen + 1 + NamespaceIDLen` with a comment is obvious. BAD-TASTE: the special-cased expression should be the general arithmetic.

issues.description: Comment on a.root contradicts its name
issues.detail: `// root property is a non-nil namespace if the "root" named policy (and only "root") is present.` — the field is now load-bearing for security; name it `rootNamespace` or `rootPolicyNS` and the comment becomes unnecessary. Good taste eliminates the need for the comment.

issues.description: ListAllNamespaces -> c.ListNamespaces call-site changes lack rationale
issues.detail: Four call sites flipped from namespaceStore.ListAllNamespaces(ctx, true) to c.ListNamespaces(ctx). The PR description says ListAllNamespaces now includes sealed namespaces — but the new c.ListNamespaces wrapper isn't shown in the diff excerpt, so the reviewer can't tell whether these call sites get the same set, a filtered set, or a different set. Spell out the semantic delta in the commit message and confirm each call site wants the new behavior (e.g., do MFA configs need to be loaded for sealed namespaces? probably no; do metric gauges? probably yes).

issues.description: Test churn ratio dwarfs production change
issues.detail: Hundreds of lines of `namespace.RootContext(nil)` -> `namespace.RootContext(t.Context())` flips and `context.Background()` -> shared ctx hoisting. Mechanically correct, individually trivial, collectively obscures the four lines in acl.go that actually change behavior. This belongs in its own commit titled 'tests: thread t.Context through namespace-aware tests' so the ACL change shows up clean in `git log -p`.
